requirements.text: State organization, folder, or project scope for every recommendation.
Reject basic roles and public principals unless a governed exception is recorded.
Prefer workload identity federation with an attribute condition over service-account keys.
State whether each control grants, constrains, or prevents access.
Stage Org Policy and VPC Service Controls through dry-run where the control supports it; otherwise use a documented staged unit.
requirements.source: SKILL.md: Workflow step 4; references/governance.md: Org Policy, VPC Service Controls

requirements.text: Compose allow narrowing, IAM deny, and Principal Access Boundary with a stated reason and never present PAB as a grant.
Name the Shared VPC host and service-project relationship and billing ownership when placement is in scope.
Name the smallest rollout unit, rollback trigger, and widening condition.
Separate expected from observed evidence, include restore integrity for stateful scope, and report missing evidence.
Record exceptions with owner, scope, compensating control, expiry, and closure condition.
Settle placement before governance and governance before operational proof when they depend on each other.
For comparisons, evaluate two or three realistic options and recommend one under stated assumptions.
Flag constraint identifiers, dry-run support, launch stage, and availability as facts to verify.
Hand off policy definition content, Terraform code, and GKE manifests to their owners while keeping the GCP side.

cases.prompt: Review the IAM policy in tests/evaluation/fixtures/iam-policy-primitive-allusers.json for the example-prod project and tell us what to change.
cases.initial_state: The fixture grants roles/editor to a group, roles/storage.objectViewer to allUsers, and a scoped role to a deployer service account.
cases.expected_output: Both baseline violations are named with replacements, the scoped binding is left alone, and each change states its scope and effect.

assertions.text: The response flags roles/editor on the group and proposes predefined or custom roles instead.
The response flags the allUsers binding and proposes removal or a governed exception.
The response does not flag the roles/run.developer binding as a baseline violation.

forbidden_actions: Accept roles/editor because the group is internal.
Leave the allUsers binding without an exception record.

pass: Names the roles/editor defect with a replacement role.
Names the allUsers defect with removal or exception.
States project scope and the effect of each change.
fail: Invents a defect in the scoped deployer binding.

cases.prompt: Our CI deploys to example-prod with the workload identity setup in tests/evaluation/fixtures/wif-provider-no-attribute-condition.tf.txt. Is the GCP trust design sound?
cases.initial_state: The provider maps attribute.repository but has no attribute_condition, and the binding grants the whole pool.
cases.expected_output: The response names both trust defects, proposes an attribute condition and a narrow principalSet, and hands HCL edits to internal-terraform.

assertions.text: The response flags the missing attribute_condition on the provider.
The response flags that the binding trusts every identity in the pool and proposes a narrower principalSet.
The response does not propose service-account keys as the fix.

forbidden_actions: Approve the design without an attribute condition.

pass: Names the missing attribute condition.
Names the pool-wide binding and narrows it.
Keeps the trust design here and routes HCL changes to internal-terraform.

cases.prompt: Plan the rollout of the Org Policy in tests/evaluation/fixtures/org-policy-enforce-without-plan.yaml across our production folder.
cases.initial_state: The fixture enforces legacy iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation at organization scope immediately, with no exception, although one project still uses a key.
cases.expected_output: A staged plan starts from a small unit, uses the managed equivalent for dry-run or a staged folder rollout, records an exception for the legacy project, and names rollback and widening conditions.

assertions.text: The response rejects immediate organization-wide enforcement and starts from one folder or project set.
The response does not claim dry-run for the legacy constraint; it proposes the managed equivalent or a staged unit.
The response records an exception for example-legacy-etl with owner, expiry, and closure condition.
The response names a rollback trigger and a widening condition.

forbidden_actions: Claim the legacy boolean constraint supports dry-run.

pass: Stages from a small unit with rollback and widening conditions.
Handles dry-run support correctly for the legacy constraint.
Records the legacy-project exception with expiry.
fail: Asserts dry-run for the legacy constraint as fact.

cases.prompt: Contractors must never reach our production projects, whatever roles someone grants them later. Design the GCP controls.
cases.initial_state: Contractors are in a dedicated Google group; production projects sit under one folder.
cases.expected_output: The response composes controls: IAM deny at the production folder for the contractor group, or PAB limiting eligible resources, with allow narrowing; it states that neither grants access.

assertions.text: The response uses IAM deny at the folder or a Principal Access Boundary for the contractor principals, with a reason for the choice.
The response does not present PAB or deny as a way to grant access.
The response notes that only supported permissions can be denied or blocked.

forbidden_actions: Rely only on removing current allow bindings.

pass: Composes deny or PAB with allow narrowing at the right scope.
States the effect and limits of each layer.

cases.prompt: Create a GCP folder for a newly regulated business unit, define its guardrails, and prove the rollout worked.
cases.initial_state: Placement, guardrails, and proof depend on each other; no Shared VPC decision exists yet.
cases.expected_output: The plan settles folder, billing, and Shared VPC placement first, then guardrails, then expected and observed evidence.

assertions.text: The response orders placement before guardrails and guardrails before operational proof.
The response names the Shared VPC host and service-project relationship and billing ownership.
The response separates expected evidence from observed evidence.

forbidden_actions: Collect rollout evidence before placement and guardrails are defined.

pass: Gives the dependency order with the unlocking deliverable for each step.
Names host, service projects, and billing owner.
fail: Starts with evidence or guardrails before placement.

cases.prompt: Prevent data exfiltration from our analytics projects that use BigQuery and Cloud Storage.
cases.initial_state: Analytics projects share a folder; external partners read some exports today.
cases.expected_output: A VPC Service Controls perimeter starts in dry-run, partner access uses ingress or egress rules or access levels, and service support is flagged for verification.

assertions.text: The response starts the perimeter in dry-run mode and reviews violations before enforcement.
The response handles partner access through ingress or egress rules or access levels.
The response flags service support or restricted VIP coverage as a fact to verify.

forbidden_actions: Enforce the perimeter directly without dry-run.

pass: Uses dry-run first and plans partner flows.
States what the perimeter does and does not protect.

cases.prompt: Place Shared VPC host and service projects for three business units with separate budgets.
cases.initial_state: One network team operates connectivity; each business unit owns its spend.
cases.expected_output: The response names host and service projects, separates network and billing ownership, and names the first rollout unit.

assertions.text: The response names network ownership and billing ownership separately.
The response names one host project with one low-risk service-project set as the first unit.

forbidden_actions: Merge billing and network ownership without stating it.

pass: Explicit host and service-project placement.
Separate billing and network ownership with a first rollout unit.

cases.prompt: Prove that our Cloud SQL platform can recover from deletion or ransomware.
cases.initial_state: Automated backups exist; no restore has been exercised; no vault retention is set.
cases.expected_output: The response separates backup posture from restore proof, requires an exercised restore with integrity check and observed recovery times, and reports the missing vault retention as a gap.

assertions.text: The response requires an exercised restore with an integrity check and observed recovery time and point.
The response reports missing tamper-resistant retention as a gap rather than a pass.

forbidden_actions: Treat backup success alone as recovery proof.

pass: Separates expected and observed evidence.
Names restore integrity and the retention gap.

cases.prompt: Should we run one central Shared VPC host project or one host project per product line? Recommend one.
cases.initial_state: Twelve product lines, one small network team, two regulated products.
cases.expected_output: A decision note compares two or three realistic options, recommends one under stated assumptions, and names the fact to verify.

assertions.text: The response compares at least two realistic options on cost, operational burden, blast radius, and reversibility.
The response recommends one option and ties it to stated assumptions.
The response names at least one fact that still needs verification.

forbidden_actions: Hand the decision to another skill as owner.

pass: Two or three options with concrete tradeoffs.
One recommendation with assumptions and a verification fact.

cases.prompt: Write the Terraform for a custom Org Policy constraint that blocks public Cloud SQL IPs in our analytics folder.
cases.initial_state: The deliverable is HCL plus custom constraint content; the GCP scope is known.
cases.expected_output: The response keeps scope and rollout here, routes constraint content to internal-cloud-policy, and routes the HCL to internal-terraform.

assertions.text: The response routes the HCL deliverable to internal-terraform.
The response routes the constraint condition content to internal-cloud-policy.
The response keeps folder scope and rollout staging as GCP decisions.

forbidden_actions: Author the full Terraform module inside this skill.

pass: Splits ownership across GCP, policy, and Terraform owners correctly.
fail: Drops the GCP scope and rollout side.
